items.title: Email Campaign · : Concierge "Year 1.5 Math" Campaign
items.preview:
**Audience:** Concierge upsell candidates (13 to 24 months post-install, not on Concierge) = **100 members**
**Why this one:** Highest-dollar conversion event available this week. These clients already survived their year-1 service, so trust is established. Recurring $99/mo revenue beats any one-time push. All 100 are past the 12-month hard floor (pre-filtered). This is a warm, high-intent list, not a cold blast.
### Subject lines (60 char max)
- **Primary (specific):** The year 1.5 question we get asked most
- **Curiosity:** Is Concierge actually worth it for you? The math.
- **Pain:** Tired of tracking your own filter swaps?
- **Authority:** What we cover so you never think about your water
- **Specific:** $99/mo: here's exactly what it includes
### Preview text (90 char max)
No pressure. Just the honest math on whether Concierge makes sense for your home.
### Body
> Hi [First Name],
>
> It's been about [X months] since we installed your water system, and now that you're past your first annual service, there's one question we hear a lot around this point:
>
> "Is this Concierge thing actually worth it for me?"
>
> Fair question. Here's the honest math, no pressure either way.
>
> Concierge is $99/mo and covers:
> - Your annual service, handled automatically
> - Filter swaps (no more tracking dates yourself)
> - Priority phone support when you need us
> - Parts coverage on your standard install components
>
> If you'd rather stay pay-as-you-go, that's completely fine. Plenty of our clients do. But if you'd rather never think about your water again, this is the simplest way to do it.
>
> Want me to check whether it pencils out for your specific setup? Just reply and I'll take a look.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: for the 5 sampled records, systems are legacy names like "Reionator Pro," "Hydronex 30c," "SorbMax Air" or "(not specified)" so every one of these uses the tenure line "It's been about [X months]..." per Rule 2. No legacy names printed.)*
### Send timing
**Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET.** Mid-morning Tuesday is the standard B2C sweet spot, and this is a considered financial decision, not an impulse click. Avoid Monday inbox-clearing.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 40 to 48%.** Tracks your 42.3% baseline. This is a genuine client list (not the broken sales-course segment), and the subject is relevant/non-promotional.
- **Click/reply: 3 to 6%.** Well above your 0.28% site-wide click avg, because this is a warm micro-segment with a reply-based CTA (lower friction than a click-through) and a concrete dollar offer.
- **Conversion: 5 to 10 enrollments** (5 to 10% of 100). Even at the low end, 5 enrollments = **$495/mo recurring / ~$5,940/yr** off one send.
### Source justification
Draws from **CONCIERGE UPSELL CONTEXT** (the "year 1.5, is it worth it, here's the math" framing and $99/mo feature list) and the **Jobber Concierge upsell candidates** trigger (pre-filtered to 13 to 24 months, respecting the 12-month hard floor in Rule 1).
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push ("30-60 Day Happy Window")
items.preview:
**Audience:** Referral push candidates (30 to 60 days post-install, satisfied) = **30 members**
**Why this one:** These clients are at peak satisfaction (new system, water noticeably better, honeymoon window) and haven't been asked for anything yet. Referrals are your cheapest acquisition channel, and Rule 3 says push referrals, not reviews. Smaller list but extremely high intent per recipient.
### Subject lines (60 char max)
- **Primary (specific):** $500 for the neighbor you send our way
- **Curiosity:** A quick thank-you (and a way to earn $500)
- **Pain:** Know someone fighting their water? We can help.
- **Authority:** Who else in your area should have water like this?
- **Specific:** Refer a neighbor, you get $500, they get an assessment
### Preview text (90 char max)
How's the water? If someone you know needs the same fix, there's $500 in it for you.
### Body
> Hi [First Name],
>
> It's been about a month since we installed your ClearWave system, and I hope the water's been treating your family right.
>
> Quick ask: if the difference has been noticeable, odds are someone you know is still dealing with the water you used to have. A neighbor, family member, coworker.
>
> Here's how our referral program works:
> - They get a free water assessment, no strings attached.
> - If they book a consult, you get a $50 gift card.
> - If they move forward and become a client, you get $500 cash.
>
> And it climbs: referrals 6 through 9 in a year are $750 each, and 10 or more are $1,000 each.
>
> Just reply with a name and the best way to reach them, or forward this email their way. We'll take it from there.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: "Katie Helbling" appears twice in the sample and "Clearwave Crest" IS a current brand name. For the opening line here I used the neutral tenure phrasing so it works across all 30 records, several of which carry legacy names like "Reionator Pro" and "Nitromax." De-dupe Katie before send.)*
### Send timing
**Thursday, 11:00 AM ET.** Late-week, late-morning. Referrals are a "feel-good, think of someone" ask that lands better when the work week pressure has eased slightly but people are still at their desks.
### Expected performance
- **Open: 45 to 52%.** Should beat baseline. Small, recently-engaged list (installed 30 to 60 days ago, your brand is top of mind) plus a dollar-figure subject line.
- **Click/reply: 8 to 15%.** Warm, recent, low-friction reply CTA. Small lists like this punch far above the 0.28% site average.
- **Conversion: 2 to 5 referral names, 1 to 2 closing** over the following 60 days. Even one close = a new system sale plus a $500 payout, net strongly positive.
### Source justification
Draws from the **REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE** (exact tiers: $500 / $750 / $1,000, and the $50 gift card for a booked-but-unclosed consult), **Rule 3** (push referrals, never reviews), **Rule 3a** (uses "free water assessment" exactly, never "water test"), and the **Jobber referral push candidates** trigger (30 to 60 days post-install, satisfied).
---
## Why only these two
I'm deliberately skipping the **1-year annual service** list (17 contacts, too small to be a standalone campaign and better handled as a Jobber transactional trigger), the **RO replacement-cycle** list (worth doing, but it's a product-reorder flow that competes for attention with Concierge this week), and the **1,000 cold leads** re-engagement (high potential, but it needs a genuine "new water news angle" hook I'd want to build properly rather than rush into the same week as two client sends).
Recommend we run **Concierge Tuesday** and **Referral Thursday**, then build the cold-lead re-engagement as next week's featured campaign with a real news hook.
Justin
CEO / ClearWave
